items.title: Section: Seven Wishes That Reality Refuses to Grant, and Eight Forms of Injury From a Household's Own Losses to Being Struck, Bound, and Cast Out

items.zh: 不隨欲苦中，復有七苦。一、欲求長壽，不隨所欲，生短壽苦。二、欲求端正，不隨所欲，生醜陋苦。三、欲生上族，不隨所欲，生下族苦。四、欲求大富，不隨所欲，生貧窮苦。五、欲求大力，不隨所欲，生羸劣苦。六、欲求了知所知境界，不隨所欲、愚癡無智現行生苦。七、欲求勝他，不隨所欲，反為他勝而生大苦。違害苦中，復有八苦。一、諸在家者，妻子等事損減生苦。二、諸出家者，貪等煩惱增益生苦。三、饑儉逼惱之所生苦。四、怨敵逼惱之所生苦；五、曠野、嶮難、迫迮逼惱之所生苦。六、繫屬於他之所生苦。七、支節不具損惱生苦。八、殺縛、斫截、捶打、驅擯逼惱生苦。
items.en: Within the suffering of wishes unfulfilled, there are, further, seven kinds: first, wishing for long life yet, contrary to that wish, meeting the suffering of an early death; second, wishing for a good appearance yet, contrary to that wish, meeting the suffering of an unattractive one; third, wishing for a high family yet, contrary to that wish, meeting the suffering of a low one; fourth, wishing for great wealth yet, contrary to that wish, meeting the suffering of poverty; fifth, wishing for great strength yet, contrary to that wish, meeting the suffering of weakness; sixth, wishing to understand what is to be known yet, contrary to that wish, meeting the suffering of ignorance persisting instead; seventh, wishing to surpass others yet, contrary to that wish, meeting the great suffering of being surpassed by them instead. Within the suffering of injury, there are, further, eight kinds: first, the suffering that arises for householders through the decline of spouse, children, and similar matters; second, the suffering that arises for renunciants through the increase of craving and similar afflictions; third, the suffering produced by the pressure of famine and hardship; fourth, the suffering produced by the pressure of hostile enemies; fifth, the suffering produced by the pressure of desolate wilderness, danger, and confinement; sixth, the suffering produced by being subject to another's control; seventh, the suffering produced by the loss and injury of one's own limbs; eighth, the suffering produced by the pressure of being killed, bound, cut, beaten, or driven out.

items.title: Section: Suffering That Relentlessly Follows — the Eight Worldly Conditions, and the Ninth, Simplest Suffering of Merely Wanting Something

items.zh: 隨逐苦中，復有九苦。依世八法有八種苦。一、壞法壞時苦，二、盡法盡時苦，三、老法老時苦，四、病法病時苦，五、死法死時苦，六、無利苦，七、無譽苦，八、有譏苦。是名八苦。九、希求苦。如是總說名隨逐苦。
items.en: Within suffering that relentlessly follows, there are, further, nine kinds. Relying on the eight worldly conditions, there are eight kinds of suffering: first, the suffering of decline, when what is subject to decline actually declines; second, the suffering of exhaustion, when what is subject to exhaustion actually runs out; third, the suffering of ageing, when what is subject to ageing actually ages; fourth, the suffering of sickness, when what is subject to sickness actually sickens; fifth, the suffering of death, when what is subject to death actually dies; sixth, the suffering of lacking benefit; seventh, the suffering of lacking reputation; eighth, the suffering of open criticism. These are called the eight sufferings. Ninth, the suffering of mere wanting. All of this together is called suffering that relentlessly follows.

items.title: Section: Suffering of Every Kind Closes the Entire Catalogue — the Shadow Cast by Five Kinds of Genuine Happiness, and the Coarse Affliction-Seeds That Make the Mind Unfit for Practice

items.zh: 一切種苦中，復有十苦。謂如前說五樂所治有五種苦。一、因苦，二、受苦，三、唯無樂苦，四、受不斷苦，五、出離、遠離、寂靜、菩提樂所對治，家、欲界結、尋、異生苦。是名五苦。復有五苦。一、逼迫苦，二、眾具匱乏苦，三、界不平等苦，四、所愛變壞苦，五、三界煩惱品麁重苦。是名五苦。前五此五，總十種苦。當知是名一切種苦。前五十五，今五十五，總有一百一十種苦，是菩薩悲所緣境界。緣此境故，諸菩薩悲生起、增長、修習圓滿。
items.en: Within suffering of every kind, there are, further, ten kinds. As already explained, the five kinds of happiness each have their own corresponding suffering as what they overcome: first, the suffering that is itself a cause; second, the suffering that is itself a felt sensation; third, the suffering of simply lacking happiness; fourth, the suffering of sensation never being cut off; fifth, the suffering overcome respectively by the happiness of renunciation, of seclusion, of stillness, and of awakening — namely, the suffering of household life, the suffering of the desire realm's own fetters, the suffering of discursive thought, and the suffering of an ordinary, unawakened being. These are called the five sufferings. There are, further, five sufferings: first, the suffering of being oppressed; second, the suffering of lacking life's requisites; third, the suffering of the body's elements falling out of balance; fourth, the suffering of what is loved changing or being destroyed; fifth, the suffering of the coarse affliction-seeds belonging to the three realms. These are called the five sufferings. The previous five together with these five make ten kinds of suffering in all; one should understand this to be called suffering of every kind. The previous fifty-five together with this fifty-five make one hundred and ten kinds of suffering in all — this is the very object upon which a bodhisattva's compassion rests. By taking this as its object, a bodhisattva's compassion arises where it had not yet arisen, grows where it had already arisen, and is brought to complete cultivation.

items.title: Section: Nineteen Kinds of Suffering — the Same Territory Distilled Into a Second, Sharper Lens for Arousing Great Compassion

items.zh: 又諸菩薩於大苦蘊，緣十九苦，發起大悲。何等名為十九種苦？一、愚癡異熟苦，二、行苦所攝苦，三、畢竟苦，四、因苦，五、生苦，六、自作逼惱苦，七、戒衰損苦，八、見衰損苦，九、宿因苦，十、廣大苦，十一、那落迦苦，十二、善趣所攝苦，十三、一切邪行所生苦，十四、一切流轉苦，十五、無智苦，十六、增長苦，十七、隨逐苦，十八、受苦，十九、麁重苦。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas, taking the great mass of suffering as their object, arouse great compassion by way of nineteen kinds of suffering. What are these nineteen kinds of suffering? First, the suffering of delusion at ripening; second, the suffering belonging to conditioning; third, the ultimate suffering; fourth, the suffering that is itself a cause; fifth, the suffering of birth; sixth, the suffering of self-inflicted distress; seventh, the suffering of declining discipline; eighth, the suffering of declining view; ninth, the suffering of past karmic cause; tenth, vast suffering; eleventh, the suffering of hell-beings; twelfth, the suffering belonging to the favourable realms; thirteenth, the suffering produced by every kind of wrong practice; fourteenth, the suffering of every kind of wandering; fifteenth, the suffering of ignorance; sixteenth, the suffering of increase; seventeenth, suffering that relentlessly follows; eighteenth, the suffering that is itself a felt sensation; nineteenth, the suffering of coarse affliction-seeds.

items.title: Section: What Makes Compassion "Great" — Depth of Object, Eons of Cultivation, Forceful Resolve Willing to Surrender a Thousand Lives, and Utter Purity

items.zh: 由四緣故，悲名大悲。一、緣甚深、微細、難了諸有情苦為境生故。二、於長時積習成故。謂諸菩薩，經於無量百千大劫積習所成。三、於所緣猛利作意而發起故。謂諸菩薩，由是作意悲所執持，為息有情眾苦因緣，尚能棄捨百千身命，況一身命及以資財。於一切種治罰大苦，為諸有情悉能堪忍。四、極清淨故。謂諸菩薩已到究竟菩薩清淨，若諸如來已到佛地如來清淨。
items.en: Through four causes and conditions, compassion is called great compassion. First, because it arises taking as its object the deep, subtle, and difficult-to-grasp suffering of sentient beings. Second, because it is accomplished through long-accumulated cultivation: bodhisattvas accomplish it across immeasurable hundreds of thousands of great eons of accumulated practice. Third, because it arises through forceful attention directed at its object: bodhisattvas, sustained by compassion through this very attention, are able, in order to bring an end to the causes and conditions of beings' many sufferings, to surrender hundreds of thousands of their own lives, let alone a single life or their own resources — and are able to bear every kind of punishing great suffering entirely for the sake of other beings. Fourth, because it is utterly pure: bodhisattvas who have reached the ultimate purity of the bodhisattva path, and Tathāgatas who have reached the purity of buddhahood itself, alone possess it in this complete form.

items.title: Section: Cultivating Great Compassion — Universal Reach, Entering the First Ground's Purified Aspiration, and Surpassing Even Noble Śrāvakas Who Have Reached the Very Summit of Their Own Path

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，由前所說百一十苦，於諸有情修悲心時，則為修習一切菩薩所有悲心。復能速證悲意樂淨，證入菩薩淨意樂地，於諸有情獲得菩薩極親厚心、極愛念心、欲作恩心、無厭惓心、代受苦心、調柔自在有堪能心。諸聖聲聞，已得證入苦諦現觀，已到究竟，於苦深遠厭俱行心相續而轉，不如菩薩於諸有情悲前行心，正觀墮在百一十種極大苦蘊。
items.en: Furthermore, when bodhisattvas cultivate compassion towards sentient beings by way of the one hundred and ten sufferings already described, this is tantamount to cultivating the compassion possessed by every bodhisattva at once. It further enables the swift attainment of a purified compassionate aspiration, entering the bodhisattva's own ground of purified aspiration, whereby one obtains, towards sentient beings, a mind of the deepest intimate closeness, a mind of the deepest cherishing, a mind wishing to bestow benefit, a mind free of weariness, a mind willing to bear their suffering in their place, and a mind gently mastered and genuinely capable. Noble śrāvakas who have already attained direct realisation of the truth of suffering, having reached the very culmination of their path, sustain a mind of deep, continuous weariness towards suffering — yet even they fall short of a bodhisattva's compassion-led mind, which correctly beholds all beings as fallen into the one hundred and ten kinds of vast suffering.

blocks.text: The catalogue closes, and the treatise defines great compassion.

"Wishing for long life, yet dying early; wishing for good looks, yet being ugly"; "wishing to surpass others, yet being surpassed". Venerable Miào Jìng: Buddhists should seek neither to surpass nor be surpassed. Eight forms of injury: a household's losses, being struck, bound, cast out.
The eight worldly conditions (decline, slander, ridicule, pain…); Master Cháng Bǎi: slander behind one's back, ridicule to one's face. And "the simplest suffering: merely wanting something".

"The five kinds of happiness each have a corresponding suffering." Venerable Miào Jìng: "there is no pain, but the absence of happiness is itself suffering." And the seeds of affliction: "they make body and mind unfit, rigid".
The same territory distilled into nineteen, for arousing great compassion. Master Cháng Bǎi: eight from the first fifty-five, eleven from the second.

Its object is "the deep, subtle, hard-to-grasp suffering of beings"; it is cultivated over aeons; its resolve is forceful: "to end the causes of beings' suffering, they can surrender hundreds of thousands of lives"; and it is utterly pure.

Cultivating compassion through these sufferings, bodhisattvas gain "deepest closeness, wishing to benefit, tirelessness". Master Cháng Bǎi: a noble śrāvaka's insight into suffering concerns himself; a bodhisattva's concerns all beings.

quiz.q: Of the seven sufferings of unfulfilled wishes, what is the seventh?
options: wishing to surpass others, yet being surpassed
quiz.why: "Seventh, wishing to surpass others, yet being surpassed by them and suffering greatly." Venerable Miào Jìng: Buddhists seek neither long life nor good looks but a mind free of afflictions — that is fundamental.

quiz.q: In relentlessly following suffering, how does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish "lack of praise" from "being criticised"?
options: criticism is being mocked and despised — slander is behind one's back, ridicule to one's face
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the suffering of being mocked and despised — slander happens behind one's back, ridicule to one's face. Venerable Miào Jìng agrees.

quiz.q: The first five sufferings of every kind correspond to which five happinesses?
options: the happiness of cause, of feeling, of counteracting pain, of ceased feeling, of non-harm
quiz.why: "The five kinds of happiness explained earlier each have a corresponding suffering." Master Cháng Bǎi lists them: the happiness of cause, of feeling, of counteracting pain, of ceased feeling, and of non-harm.

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain "the suffering of the coarse heaviness of afflictions in the three realms"?
options: the seeds of affliction are also suffering; they make body and mind unfit, rigid, untamed
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the seeds of affliction are themselves suffering. Master Cháng Bǎi: they make body and mind unfit, rigid, and untamed.

quiz.q: How do the lectures relate the nineteen sufferings to the hundred and ten?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the first eight from the first fifty-five, the last eleven from the second; Miào Jìng: all re-drawn from the hundred and ten as the more important ones
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: of the nineteen, the first eight come from the first fifty-five, the last eleven from the second fifty-five. Venerable Miào Jìng: all are re-drawn from the hundred and ten, meaning these are the more important ones.

quiz.q: In the third of the four causes of great compassion, how many lives can a bodhisattva surrender to end beings' suffering?
options: hundreds of thousands of lives, let alone one life or wealth
quiz.why: "To end the causes of beings' suffering, they can surrender hundreds of thousands of lives, let alone a single life or their resources." Venerable Miào Jìng: this shows how great a bodhisattva is — who would be willing to be one!

quiz.q: "A mind bearing suffering in their place" — how does Venerable Miào Jìng view it?
options: bodhisattvas literally take on beings' karma
it expresses the vastness of compassion — one cannot actually suffer in beings' place
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: it expresses how especially vast a bodhisattva's compassion is — in reality one cannot suffer in beings' place. The literal English may suggest a real transfer.
